examples.description: Inspect your server-authenticated identity; available to every active user.
examples.sql: SHOW CURRENT USER;

examples.description: List effective action capabilities; this is not a list of every readable document.
examples.sql: SHOW CURRENT USER PRIVILEGES;

examples.description: Read the identity/user/role/key catalog revision; administrative authority required.
examples.sql: SHOW SECURITY REVISION;

examples.description: Read the collection catalog revision; designated installation administrator required.
examples.sql: SHOW CATALOG REVISION;

examples.description: Create a deny-all two-dimensional collection. Initially no ingest template exists.
examples.sql: CREATE PROTECTED COLLECTION docs DIM 2 METRIC cosine;

examples.description: Enable graph storage on the newly created empty collection at its current security revision.
examples.sql: ALTER COLLECTION docs SET GRAPH ENABLED IF REVISION 1;

examples.description: Configure an unweighted edge type after graph enablement advances the collection security revision.
examples.sql: ALTER COLLECTION docs SET EDGE TYPE cites IF REVISION 2;

examples.description: Read the policy/ACL/label revision for this collection, not the identity revision.
examples.sql: SHOW SECURITY REVISION ON COLLECTION docs;

examples.description: Inspect policy and its revision before replacing it.
examples.sql: SHOW COLLECTION docs SECURITY POLICY;

examples.description: Replace the whole typed policy. Preserve required templates when editing; this is not a partial merge.
Create a role with zero permissions; its name has no special meaning.
examples.sql: CREATE ROLE finance_reader;

examples.description: Allow read operations and dense search on the exact active docs incarnation.
examples.sql: GRANT READ, SEARCH ON COLLECTION docs TO ROLE finance_reader;

examples.description: Both department and clearance are required. The new user is active but has no key or privileges.
examples.sql: CREATE USER ana SET DEPARTMENT Finance SET CLEARANCE CONFIDENTIAL;

examples.description: Assign the existing role to the existing user.
examples.sql: GRANT ROLE finance_reader TO USER ana;

examples.description: Inspect the role capability grants.
examples.sql: SHOW ROLE finance_reader PRIVILEGES;

examples.description: List role names; membership is requested separately with WITH USERS.
examples.sql: SHOW ROLES;

examples.description: List roles and their user names.
examples.sql: SHOW ROLES WITH USERS;

examples.description: List users, trusted attributes, enabled status, and role names.
examples.sql: SHOW USERS;

examples.description: Create a separate ingestion role.
examples.sql: CREATE ROLE ingestion_writer;

examples.description: Raw vector/source ingestion requires INGEST as well as CREATE/UPDATE.
examples.sql: GRANT READ, SEARCH, CREATE, INGEST, UPDATE, DELETE ON COLLECTION docs TO ROLE ingestion_writer;

examples.description: The ingestion principal has sufficient clearance to ingest the trusted templates.
examples.sql: CREATE USER writer SET DEPARTMENT Ingestion SET CLEARANCE RESTRICTED;

examples.description: Give the ingestion user only the defined writer role.
examples.sql: GRANT ROLE ingestion_writer TO USER writer;

examples.description: Create an operations role independently of the security administrator.
examples.sql: CREATE ROLE operations;

examples.description: ON SYSTEM is for installation actions. OBSERVE permits operator metrics, not document access.
examples.sql: GRANT OBSERVE ON SYSTEM TO ROLE operations;

examples.description: Create an operator identity.
examples.sql: CREATE USER ops SET DEPARTMENT Operations SET CLEARANCE INTERNAL;

examples.description: Assign observation privileges.
examples.sql: GRANT ROLE operations TO USER ops;

examples.description: Create a separate HR role.
examples.sql: CREATE ROLE hr_reader;

examples.description: Object policy still separates HR from Finance despite the same collection capability.
examples.sql: GRANT READ, SEARCH ON COLLECTION docs TO ROLE hr_reader;

examples.description: Create the HR reader.
examples.sql: CREATE USER ben SET DEPARTMENT HR SET CLEARANCE INTERNAL;

examples.description: Assign the HR reader role.
examples.sql: GRANT ROLE hr_reader TO USER ben;

examples.description: Use CLI --key-out with a new private filename. No secret is printed; each issuance creates a new credential.
examples.sql: ISSUE API KEY FOR USER writer;

examples.description: Use CLI --key-out with a new private filename. No secret is printed; each issuance creates a new credential.
examples.sql: ISSUE API KEY FOR USER ana;

examples.description: Use CLI --key-out with a new private filename. No secret is printed; each issuance creates a new credential.
examples.sql: ISSUE API KEY FOR USER ben;

examples.description: Use CLI --key-out with a new private filename. No secret is printed; each issuance creates a new credential.
examples.sql: ISSUE API KEY FOR USER ops;

examples.description: List credential IDs and revocation status only; no secret or hash is recoverable here.
examples.sql: SHOW API KEYS FOR USER ana;

examples.description: Run as writer. Save the returned ID as POINT_ID; do not send an id field on create.
examples.sql: CREATE POINTS INTO docs USING TEMPLATE finance {vector:[1,0],payload:{text:'finance report'}} REQUEST 'manual-finance-001';

examples.description: Point objects are comma-separated without an outer array. Save the two returned IDs as SECOND_ID and THIRD_ID.
examples.sql: CREATE POINTS INTO docs USING TEMPLATE finance {vector:[0,1],payload:{text:'second report'}}, {vector:[1,1],payload:{text:'third report'}} REQUEST 'manual-finance-002';

examples.description: The trusted template determines the department; it is not supplied as an authoritative payload field.
examples.sql: CREATE POINTS INTO docs USING TEMPLATE hr {vector:[0,1],payload:{text:'hr policy'}} REQUEST 'manual-hr-001';

examples.description: Same principal, request ID and identical content returns the original IDs after reauthorization; it must not insert a duplicate.
examples.sql: CREATE POINTS INTO docs USING TEMPLATE finance {vector:[1,0],payload:{text:'finance report'}} REQUEST 'manual-finance-001';

examples.description: Use a real server-assigned ID. Hidden and missing IDs both yield no readable rows.
examples.sql: GET docs POINTS 'POINT_ID';

examples.description: Retrieve multiple IDs under the same access domain.
examples.sql: GET docs POINTS 'POINT_ID', 'SECOND_ID';

examples.description: Finance sees its three documents, not the HR document.
examples.sql: COUNT docs;

examples.description: Query permission on /text is required, independently of permission to read it.
examples.sql: COUNT docs WHERE text = 'finance report';

examples.description: Read an authorized page. For pagination use the response next cursor, not a numeric offset.
examples.sql: SCROLL docs LIMIT 2;

examples.description: Replace CURSOR_ID with the preceding response next cursor.
examples.sql: SCROLL docs AFTER 'CURSOR_ID' LIMIT 2;

examples.description: Inline vectors must match the collection dimension. The result contains only authorized points.
examples.sql: SEARCH docs NEAR [1,0] LIMIT 10 WITH PAYLOAD;

examples.description: Filter fields require query permission; budget cannot increase the server ceiling.
examples.sql: SEARCH docs NEAR [1,0] WHERE text CONTAINS 'finance' LIMIT 2 BUDGET 1000 WITH PAYLOAD;

examples.description: Session collection selection requires Read on the collection. It does not grant access.
examples.sql: USE docs;

examples.description: Replace an authorized existing object using its server ID; this is not a payload patch.
examples.sql: UPDATE POINTS IN docs {id:'POINT_ID',vector:[1,0],payload:{text:'updated finance report'}};

examples.description: A mixed unauthorized explicit batch is rejected atomically.
examples.sql: UPDATE POINTS IN docs {id:'SECOND_ID',vector:[0,1],payload:{text:'obsolete'}}, {id:'THIRD_ID',vector:[1,1],payload:{text:'third revised'}};

examples.description: Explicit IDs need Delete permission; read permission alone never permits deletion.
examples.sql: DELETE FROM docs POINTS 'THIRD_ID';

examples.description: Requires confirmation (CLI --yes in scripts); selection uses the delete-authorized domain. Protected preview omits counts.
examples.sql: DELETE FROM docs WHERE text = 'obsolete';

examples.description: An explicit object grant can share across departments in the same tenant. READ does not automatically grant SEARCH.
examples.sql: GRANT READ, SEARCH ON POINT 'POINT_ID' IN docs TO USER ben;

examples.description: Explicit deny overrides the permit, role and department. It does not raise clearance.
examples.sql: DENY READ, SEARCH ON POINT 'POINT_ID' IN docs TO USER ben;

examples.description: Remove the deny while keeping the independent explicit permit.
examples.sql: REVOKE DENY READ, SEARCH ON POINT 'POINT_ID' IN docs FROM USER ben;

examples.description: Remove the explicit permit. Department/owner/group/inherited permits may still apply.
examples.sql: REVOKE GRANT READ, SEARCH ON POINT 'POINT_ID' IN docs FROM USER ben;

examples.description: Conditional syntax: payroll must already exist in the trusted identity authority. Group creation/membership has no ChironQL command in 1.3.
examples.sql: GRANT READ ON POINT 'POINT_ID' IN docs TO GROUP payroll;

examples.description: Conditional syntax: payroll must already exist in the trusted identity authority. Group creation/membership has no ChironQL command in 1.3.
examples.sql: DENY READ ON POINT 'POINT_ID' IN docs TO GROUP payroll;

examples.description: Conditional syntax: payroll must already exist in the trusted identity authority. Group creation/membership has no ChironQL command in 1.3.
examples.sql: REVOKE GRANT READ ON POINT 'POINT_ID' IN docs FROM GROUP payroll;

examples.description: Conditional syntax: payroll must already exist in the trusted identity authority. Group creation/membership has no ChironQL command in 1.3.
examples.sql: REVOKE DENY READ ON POINT 'POINT_ID' IN docs FROM GROUP payroll;

examples.description: Owner is resolved to an immutable user ID. Content writers cannot change this by editing payload.
examples.sql: ALTER POINT 'POINT_ID' IN docs SET OWNER ana;

examples.description: Changing the security department can change visibility; LabelsManage/delegation checks apply.
examples.sql: ALTER POINT 'POINT_ID' IN docs SET DEPARTMENT HR;

examples.description: Raising classification also tightens derived representation labels; existing lower-clearance readers lose access.
examples.sql: ALTER POINT 'POINT_ID' IN docs SET CLASSIFICATION RESTRICTED;

examples.description: Several distinct SET clauses are one security transaction. Duplicate SET attributes are rejected.
examples.sql: ALTER POINT 'POINT_ID' IN docs SET OWNER writer SET DEPARTMENT Finance SET CLASSIFICATION RESTRICTED;

examples.description: Changes trusted identity attributes and drains the old authorization context.
examples.sql: ALTER USER ana SET DEPARTMENT Finance;

examples.description: A role does not change clearance; explicit identity administration does.
examples.sql: ALTER USER ana SET CLEARANCE INTERNAL;

examples.description: Requires confirmation; existing credentials stop authenticating while suspended.
examples.sql: ALTER USER ana SET STATUS SUSPENDED;

examples.description: Reactivate the identity; revoked credentials remain revoked.
examples.sql: ALTER USER ana SET STATUS ACTIVE;

examples.description: Apply several distinct identity attributes in one transaction.
examples.sql: ALTER USER ana SET DEPARTMENT Finance SET CLEARANCE CONFIDENTIAL SET STATUS ACTIVE;

examples.description: Replace KEY_ID with the ID from SHOW API KEYS. Requires --key-out pointing to a new file; the old credential is revoked.
examples.sql: ROTATE API KEY 'KEY_ID';

examples.description: Use the new credential ID for this example. Revocation cannot be undone by reactivating a user.
examples.sql: REVOKE API KEY 'ROTATED_KEY_ID';

examples.description: Remove membership without deleting the role or user; existing sessions observe revocation.
examples.sql: REVOKE ROLE finance_reader FROM USER ana;

examples.description: Edit the role itself; this affects every member, unlike REVOKE ROLE ... FROM USER.
examples.sql: REVOKE SEARCH ON COLLECTION docs FROM ROLE finance_reader;

examples.description: Remove the installation action from all members of the role.
examples.sql: REVOKE OBSERVE ON SYSTEM FROM ROLE operations;

examples.description: Only the display name changes; ID, ownership and grants retain identity.
examples.sql: RENAME USER ana TO ana_archive;

examples.description: Renaming preserves the internal role ID and memberships.
examples.sql: RENAME ROLE finance_reader TO finance_viewer;

examples.description: Requires confirmation. Recreating the same name never restores old grants/memberships.
examples.sql: DROP ROLE finance_viewer;

examples.description: Requires confirmation; retire the user and revoke credentials. Existing object ownership is not transferred.
examples.sql: DROP USER ana_archive;

examples.description: Use the current value returned by SHOW SECURITY REVISION. Here 9 is illustrative, not a reusable token.
examples.sql: CREATE ROLE revision_guard IF REVISION 9;

examples.description: Intentional conflict: revision zero is stale on an initialized installation. No role is created.
examples.sql: CREATE ROLE stale_example IF REVISION 0;

examples.description: Identity management is bootstrap authority; this parses but authorization rejects it.
examples.sql: GRANT IDENTITY_MANAGE ON SYSTEM TO ROLE operations;

examples.description: Protected collections reject client-ID UPSERT; use CREATE POINTS or UPDATE POINTS.
examples.sql: UPSERT INTO docs {id:'chosen',vector:[1,0],payload:{text:'wrong create API'}};

examples.description: Legacy collection creation; protected installations require CREATE PROTECTED COLLECTION.
examples.sql: CREATE COLLECTION products DIM 3 METRIC cosine WITH {named_vector_dims:{image:3}};

examples.description: Alternative Euclidean distance metric.
examples.sql: CREATE COLLECTION euclidean DIM 3 METRIC l2;

examples.description: Alternative dot-product metric.
examples.sql: CREATE COLLECTION dot_products DIM 3 METRIC dot;

examples.description: Explicit client IDs and asynchronous WAL acknowledgement on the legacy surface.
examples.sql: UPSERT INTO products {id:'phone',vector:[1,0,0],vectors:{image:[0,1,0]},payload:{category:'electronics',price:699,title:'wireless phone',meta:{brand:'acme'}}}, {id:'book',vector:[0,1,0],payload:{category:'books',price:25}} NO WAIT;

examples.description: All ordinary search control clauses; RECALL is a target, not a measured result. Protected dense search uses exact evaluation.
examples.sql: SEARCH products NEAR [1,0,0] LIMIT 5 WITH PAYLOAD EF 64 RECALL 0.95 BUDGET 1000;

examples.description: Stored-vector references require a readable existing point; unavailable on protected ChironQL.
examples.sql: SEARCH products NEAR @phone LIMIT 5;

examples.description: Named vector space must be configured and populated.
examples.sql: SEARCH products NEAR @phone USING image LIMIT 5;

examples.description: Equality, conjunction and a bounded numeric range.
examples.sql: SEARCH products NEAR [1,0,0] WHERE category = 'electronics' AND price >= 100 AND price <= 700 LIMIT 5;

examples.description: Not-equal and strict numeric comparisons.
examples.sql: COUNT products WHERE category != 'books' AND price > 100 AND price < 1000;

examples.description: Single-field membership implements a disjunction without OR.
examples.sql: SCROLL products WHERE category IN ['electronics','books'] LIMIT 10;

examples.description: Token intersection on a string field.
examples.sql: COUNT products WHERE title CONTAINS 'wireless phone';

examples.description: Dotted nested payload path.
examples.sql: COUNT products WHERE meta.brand = 'acme';

examples.description: Numeric sparse-vector fusion; TEXT is not a natural-language string or the native BM25 API.
examples.sql: HYBRID products NEAR [1,0,0] TEXT {12:1.2,98:0.7} FUSION rrf LIMIT 5;

examples.description: Explicit dense/sparse weights.
examples.sql: HYBRID products NEAR [1,0,0] TEXT {12:1.2} FUSION weighted DENSE 0.7 SPARSE 0.3 LIMIT 5;

examples.description: Named-vector hybrid with query filter.
examples.sql: HYBRID products NEAR [0,1,0] USING image TEXT {12:1} WHERE price <= 700 LIMIT 5;

examples.description: Fuse multiple dense query vectors with matching weights.
examples.sql: MULTI products NEAR [1,0,0], NEAR [0,1,0] FUSION weighted WEIGHTS 0.6,0.4 LIMIT 5;

examples.description: RRF multi-query fusion.
examples.sql: MULTI products NEAR [1,0,0], NEAR [0,1,0] FUSION rrf WHERE price <= 700 LIMIT 5;

examples.description: Positive and negative examples; existing points required.
examples.sql: RECOMMEND products LIKE phone UNLIKE book LIMIT 5;

examples.description: Named-space recommendation.
examples.sql: RECOMMEND products LIKE phone USING image WHERE price <= 700 LIMIT 5;

examples.description: Count matches on legacy authorization surface.
examples.sql: COUNT products;

examples.description: ID-based cursor; use the previous response cursor.
examples.sql: SCROLL products AFTER 'phone' LIMIT 20;

examples.description: Batch point retrieval.
examples.sql: GET products POINTS phone, book;

examples.description: Not exposed by protected ChironQL; use known protected collection names.
examples.sql: SHOW COLLECTIONS;

examples.description: Legacy schema/config inspection; protected policy has SHOW COLLECTION ... SECURITY POLICY.
examples.sql: DESCRIBE products;

examples.description: Merge ordinary payload fields; protected partial update is not supported.
examples.sql: UPDATE products POINT phone SET PAYLOAD {featured:true};

examples.description: Replace the legacy payload object.
examples.sql: UPDATE products POINT phone SET PAYLOAD {category:'electronics',price:699} REPLACE;

examples.description: Explicit ID deletion.
examples.sql: DELETE FROM products POINTS phone, book;

examples.description: Filtered deletion requires confirmation; legacy preview counts matches.
examples.sql: DELETE FROM products WHERE category = 'archived';

examples.description: Requires graph lifecycle and edge-type setup via a native administrative API.
examples.sql: RELATE products phone -> related_to -> book SET {strength:0.8} IDEMPOTENCY KEY 'relation-001' NO WAIT;

examples.description: Conditional: requires a server-bound deferred session; stateless requests reject it.
examples.sql: RELATE products phone -> related_to -> book WITH DEFERRED ENDPOINTS;

examples.description: Replace EDGE_ID with a returned opaque edge token, not a point ID.
examples.sql: UNRELATE products EDGE 'EDGE_ID' NO WAIT;

examples.description: Merge edge properties.
examples.sql: UPDATE products EDGE 'EDGE_ID' SET PROPERTIES {strength:0.9} NO WAIT;

examples.description: Replace edge properties.
examples.sql: UPDATE products EDGE 'EDGE_ID' SET PROPERTIES {strength:0.9} REPLACE NO WAIT;

examples.description: Exact traversal, requires enabled graph.
examples.sql: TRAVERSE products FROM phone VIA related_to DIRECTION OUT DEPTH 2 LIMIT 20 WITH PAYLOAD RETURN NODES;

examples.description: Incoming edges with a property filter.
examples.sql: TRAVERSE products FROM phone DIRECTION IN DEPTH 1 EDGE WHERE strength >= 0.5 LIMIT 20 RETURN EDGES;

examples.description: Simple paths require LIMIT; WHERE is not a protected security policy.
examples.sql: TRAVERSE products FROM phone, book VIA related_to DIRECTION ANY DEPTH 2 WHERE price <= 700 EDGE WHERE strength >= 0.5 BUDGET 1000 MS LIMIT 20 WITH PAYLOAD RETURN PATHS;

examples.description: Graph-constrained search; ALLOW DEGRADED does not bypass authorization.
examples.sql: SEARCH products NEAR [1,0,0] CONNECTED TO phone VIA related_to DIRECTION OUT WITHIN 2 HOPS ALLOW DEGRADED LIMIT 10;

examples.description: Graph-constrained numeric hybrid.
examples.sql: HYBRID products NEAR [1,0,0] TEXT {12:1} CONNECTED TO phone VIA related_to DIRECTION ANY WITHIN 2 HOPS ALLOW DEGRADED LIMIT 10;

examples.description: Destructive legacy lifecycle operation; protected drop remains rejected.
examples.sql: DROP COLLECTION products;

examples.description: Equivalent placement of IF EXISTS before the collection name.
examples.sql: DROP COLLECTION IF EXISTS products;

examples.description: Suppress a missing legacy collection error, not authorization errors.
examples.sql: DROP COLLECTION products IF EXISTS;

examples.description: Set the session collection.
examples.sql: USE products;

examples.description: Run after USE products in the same session or pass --collection products.
examples.sql: SEARCH NEAR [1,0,0] LIMIT 5;
